<reason>B won a competitive debate by forcing the motion’s conjunction: parity-as-fact plus policy that “reflects that evidence.” A’s confound attack was sharp, and B never fully isolated parental sex from biology and formation pathways, but A admitted there is no large representative stable-from-birth cell. B used that as the live burden, treating “control away the pathway” as editing the average the motion asks about, while still conceding no child should wait in care.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s Rebuttal 2/closing: A’s “not in the form those files allow” became a concession that representative planned-from-birth parity is missing, so law would be presuming the claim rather than reflecting it.</best_rebuttal>
